tools.name: word.info
tools.description: Inspect a document in your workspace (docx, md, html, rtf, odt, txt or json): pages, words, paragraphs, sections, comments and document properties. Reads only. `path` is relative to your workspace, the folder your own file tools (list_dir, read_file) see; files outside it cannot be named.

tools.name: word.text
tools.description: Extract the plain text of a document in your workspace, with its word and paragraph counts. Reads only. `path` is relative to your workspace (see word.info). A very long document can exceed the answer size limit; word.inspect with text false gives its structure instead.

tools.name: word.inspect
tools.description: Inspect a document's structure in your workspace: its blocks (paragraphs with style and runs, tables with cells), with their text unless `text` is false. Reads only. `path` is relative to your workspace (see word.info).

tools.name: word.convert
tools.description: Convert a document in your workspace and write the result there: docx, md, html, rtf, odt, txt, json, pdf or png, chosen by `format` or else by the extension of `out`. Both paths are relative to your workspace (see word.info); nothing is written outside it, and a file already at `out` is never replaced: choose a new name.

tools.name: word.new
tools.description: Write a new document into your workspace from plain text: each line becomes a paragraph, with an optional title property. The extension of `out` picks the format, usually .docx. `out` is relative to your workspace (see word.info); nothing is written outside it, and a file already at `out` is never replaced: choose a new name.
